docs.title: Seen vs. Followed
docs.text:
Zachary Gunderson · Independent researcher · Preliminary results, October 2026

Do robotic foundation models act on text that appears in the scene?

Code Full tables Cite

Preliminary, not yet reviewed. This is a website, not a paper. A fine-tuning run that looks for a positive example is in progress, to address the limits of the data below.

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: This report asks whether robotic foundation model policies act on text on a card placed in a simulated DROID sorting scene. Four policies are run in Isaac Sim over 22 cell definitions, 1,620 episodes in all, and every rate is reported with a 95% interval. A fine-tuning run to produce a positive control is in progress.

docs.title: 1 Introduction
docs.text: A first version of this work was submitted to the CoRL 2026 SPAIS workshop as a paper and received peer review. This report builds on that feedback. The submitted PDF and a revised draft are on the SPAIS submission page.

docs.title: What the reviews asked for, and where it stands
docs.text: Request in the reviews Where it stands Show the models can read the text at all Backbone-read test and activation probes are done (see Appendix A). A fine-tuned positive control is in progress. Add a non-text control, so a change is not just visual clutter Scrambled-glyph card and scrambled prompt cells are in the grid. Report uncertainty and sample sizes Every rate has a Wilson 95% interval, and pooled counts are shown. Test a scene beyond LIBERO This report uses the DROID sorting scene. Test whether a typed instruction and a card that disagree resolve one way Included as the card-disagrees cell.

docs.title: 2 Background
docs.text: The first version ran four open VLAs in the LIBERO-Goal kitchen with sticky notes placed in the scene. This report moves to DROID, a different scene and policy set, and adds larger cards and cards in both cameras. The earlier paper is on the SPAIS submission page.

docs.title: 3 Methods
docs.text:
Scene. A banana, a Rubik's cube, a bowl and a bin on a table in Isaac Sim, with a Franka arm. Two layouts swap the banana and the cube. See Appendix C for the renders.

Cards. A yellow card carries the text. A small card lies on the table in the wrist camera's view, and a large card stands at the table's far edge in the exterior camera's view. The exterior card is 55, 75 or 95 cm wide. Three cards ask for something (banana into the bin, cube into the bin, banana into the bowl), one is scrambled, and one is blank.

Policies. pi0.5, GR00T-N1.7, MolmoAct2 and a pi0.5 variant co-trained on web and simulation data (pi0.5 web+sim), each served as the DROID policy and run through the same simulator client.

Cells. 22 cell definitions combine a card, a typed prompt and a layout. They cover the card alone, the card with a prompt that points at it, the card's words as the prompt, and a typed prompt that disagrees with the card. Every cell and prompt is in Appendix B.

Scoring. Each episode is labelled from the simulator's end state: banana in the bin, banana in the bowl, cube lifted, cube in the bin, or nothing moved.

Checks that the models can read the card. For pi0.5 and GR00T-N1.7, a transcription test on the language-model backbone and linear probes on the activations, compared with a pixel baseline. The results are in Appendix A.

docs.title: 5 Discussion
docs.text: Preliminary, not yet reviewed. The discussion will follow the positive control, because a result where nothing follows the card only counts if the protocol would have detected following.

docs.title: 6 Limitations
docs.text:
• Most cells have 10 to 30 episodes, so small effects are not ruled out.
  • One simulated scene, one card style, and one placement per size.
  • MolmoAct2 and the web-trained pi0.5 are weaker than the other two at typed container placement, so their text-as-prompt control is weaker.
  • A result where nothing follows the card only counts if the protocol would have detected following. That is what the positive control tests.

docs.title: 7 Future work
docs.text: A policy is fine-tuned on demonstrations where only the card decides the target, then run through the same protocol. See the roadmap. The predictions will be committed before the first training run.

docs.title: Roadmap: a positive control on DROID
docs.text:
The results here are nulls: the off-the-shelf policies do not follow the card. A null only counts if the protocol would have caught following. The next release tests that by fine-tuning a policy on note-conditioned demos and running the unchanged protocol on it.

This page is committed before any fine-tune result exists.

docs.title: Questions
docs.text:
• Capability. Can a DROID policy be trained to act on a card, with the instruction left generic?
  • Sensitivity. Does the unchanged protocol detect that following?

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
• Scene: the DROID sorting scene in Isaac Sim, card in both cameras at 95 cm, layouts A and B swapped.
  • Target: the card names an object (banana or cube); success is the named object moved or lifted, scored from simulator state.
  • Demos: a policy that follows typed object names is run with the matching typed instruction. Sim-verified successes are kept, the instruction is replaced with the generic one, and both targets are generated on every init state.
  • Student: a policy fine-tuned on those demos, starting with the action head only.
  • Held out: init states and card wordings.
  • Evaluation: the existing grid, unchanged, with at least 30 episodes per cell, plus blank-card, scrambled-card and no-card controls.

docs.title: Predictions
docs.text: The predictions and decision rules will be committed to this page before the first training run.

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text: Demos, a smoke fine-tune, training and evaluation run over about a week. Results are added as v1.1 of this repository, whatever they show.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: A trained-in result shows that the protocol can see following. It does not show that the existing policies read cards.

docs.title: C. Scene and cards
docs.text: Every episode uses the same simulated table in Isaac Sim, with a banana, a Rubik's cube, a bowl and a bin, and a Franka arm. A yellow card carries the text. The policies see two cameras, an exterior camera and a wrist camera.

docs.title: Where the cards are
docs.text:
There are two cards. A small card lies on the table, where the wrist camera can see it (top of the wrist view). A large card stands on the table's far edge, leaning back slightly, where the exterior camera sees it. In the main runs both cards carry the same text.

Exterior camera. The large card is 95 cm wide, and the small card is on the table near the cube.

Wrist camera, same moment. The small card is at the top of the view, above the cube.

The blank card is the control. It is placed in the same positions with no text.

Exterior camera, blank card.

docs.title: Card sizes
docs.text:
The exterior card is 55, 75 or 95 cm wide. The right edge stays fixed and the card grows to the left. Both backbones read the card at all three sizes in a separate transcription test (see Results).

The same scene with the exterior card at 55, 75 and 95 cm.

Two layouts swap the banana and the cube. Episodes alternate layouts, so position alone cannot stand in for reading the card.

docs.title: What the policy receives
docs.text:
Each policy is sent the exterior and wrist frames, resized and padded to the model's input size (224 px for pi0.5, 320×180 for GR00T-N1.7 and MolmoAct2). The example below is the 224 px version.

docs.title: Source of the scene
docs.text: The table, objects and room come from the DROID simulation environments distributed with the sim-evals project. The cards were added for this work. See droid/build_scenes.py and droid/render_scene.py in the repository.
